Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

among preposition

also amongst, amid, amidst

classical

Ov. Met. 1.304: nat lupus inter ovēs
Liv. 2.13.6: inter tēla hostium Tiberim trānāvit

inter (+ accusative)

preposition with the accusative

among, amid

In the midst of a number of things or people: inter ovēs, among the sheep. Inter sē, among themselves, each other: amant inter sē.

Other words

  • apud (+ accusative) — among (a people), in the eyes of

    preposition with the accusative · also used · classical · Cic. Flacc. 31: hoc est apud Graecōs … glōriōsius quam Rōmae triumphāsse

    Among a people, in their land or in their opinion: apud Graecōs, among the Greeks (see at the house of).

  • in (+ ablative) — among (one of a number)

    preposition with the ablative · also used · classical · Verg. E. 8.56: Orpheus in silvīs, inter delphīnas Arīōn

    Of one among many: in prīmīs, among the first, above all.

Examples

  • nat lupus inter ovēs, fulvōs vehit unda leōnēs

    the wolf swims among the sheep, the water carries tawny lionsOv. Met. 1.304

  • Orpheus in silvīs, inter delphīnas Arīōn

    an Orpheus in the woods, an Arion among the dolphinsVerg. E. 8.56

  • Cloelia virgō ūna ex obsidibus … dux agminis virginum inter tēla hostium Tiberim trānāvit

    the girl Cloelia, one of the hostages, … at the head of a band of girls swam the Tiber amid the enemy’s spearsLiv. 2.13.6

  • sūcinum, quod ipsī glēsum vocant, inter vada atque in ipsō lītore legunt

    they gather amber, which they call glesum, among the shallows and on the shore itselfTac. Germ. 45.4

  • Cicerōnēs puerī amant inter sē, exercentur, sed discunt

    the two Cicero boys love each other and play games, but they do learnCic. Att. 6.1.12

See also between, in, at the house of.
